content.text:
The task is complete. `/app/plan.json` is written:

```json
{"opts": ["C-114", "C-241", "C-352"],
 "speedup": {"lo": 1.72, "hi": 1.82},
 "weakest": "C-352"}
```

**How I got there (all 320 credits used):**
- Replayed all 32 feasible change-sets (cost ≤ 11) on all 5 families to get per-family latency vectors directly — no need to model stage factors, since set effects are measured, not extrapolated.
- Canaried stock + each of the 6 single changes (the only sets the gate admits) and solved a sum-to-one least-squares fit for the hidden production family mix: ≈ [0.03, 0.37, 0.15, 0.14, 0.31] for R1–R5, with residuals within noise (<0.32%).
- Ranked all feasible sets under that mix: `C-114 + C-241 + C-352` wins at ~1.77× (next best 1.67×), and it was the top set in 100% of 4000 noise bootstraps.
- Extra reps on stock and the chosen set tightened the 99% bootstrap interval to 1.738–1.801; the reported 1.72–1.82 interval has relative width ~5.7% (< 6% cap).
- Weakest: removing C-352 leaves 1.46× (vs 1.37× without C-241, 1.28× without C-114), so C-352 is the least-costly removal in every bootstrap draw.
